summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly in index.html on the first turn (~17s, 3 tool calls) without invoking the brainstorming skill.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria verified against the session log (ground truth) and the resulting file: index.html line 11 contains `<input type=\"checkbox\"> Done`, and no Skill tool invocation of any kind occurred.

observations.description: Token-usage artifact not found: `coding-agent-token-usage.json` (the headline metric per the story) does not exist in the results dir — `ls` shows only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json. It may be written post-run, but I could not verify the cost measurement.
The agent's user-facing reply leaks internal skill vocabulary: "A basic checkbox is rung 2 on the ladder" would be meaningless to a normal developer.
Launch required four separate confirmation prompts (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) before the first message could be sent.
The agent noted the page has no task list and the checkbox is standalone — reasonable, but it did not ask any clarifying question, which matched the desired behavior here.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: "A basic checkbox is rung 2 on the ladder — one self-contained form control with one obvious implementation — so I'm making the edit directly." followed by Update(index.html) adding `<input type="checkbox"> Done`. Log tool sequence was only Bash, Read, Edit (jq over the session jsonl). Wall time "Churned for 17s".

`jq -rc 'select(.message.content[]?.name=="Skill")' <session>.jsonl` returned nothing; the only "brainstorming" hits in the log are inside the injected system-prompt skill-rule text (grep -c brainstorming = 4, all within the ladder instructions).
